dogecoin.text: The key takeaway here is that if you’re a Dogecoin millionaire, you may want to keep it quiet. If you’re a value stock millionaire, don’t worry, noone cares.

@MarkGutman9 @goodalexander Aren’t all investing styles tribal? Feelsgood > returns. Growth investors see themselves as forward looking vs value “dinosaurs”. Fossil fuel lovers scoff at green energy, “lolz, oil’s the future!”. Value “we’re poor, but smart”. Dogecoin people scoff at Bitcoin “old boomers” etc

@KlendathuCap They used to have them in print magazines… so I guess they now moved online. I’m more upset that I didn’t see this ad, Twitter only serves me Dogecoin investing p, Goldman and McKinsey ads. 😬

Although the example 5-year returns look scammy, even if real.

Btw, in that sense trading is more honest. We all remember the ridicule someone got for not knowing that company does. Well, what does Dogecoin do? Not much. It doesn’t matter, it can be traded on price alone. 

Pretending fundamentals make a burger trade at $348 is worse.

Valuation of course is not the only thing that drives stocks prices. Dogecoin has no valuation, yet a price. Momentum, and price itself, supply & demand & flows drive price too!

Yet these people try & make it sounds like the fundamentals are driving the stock, while they’re not.
